stem: M is the centre of a circle. D and E are two points on the circle, and the straight line ED is extended outside the circle to a point A, so that D lies between E and A. The length DA is equal to the radius MD, and the measure of angle $MAD$ is ${=p}^\circ$. Find the measure of angle $AME$ in degrees.
solution: Since $DA = MD$, triangle $MDA$ is isosceles, so angle $AMD$ = angle $MAD$ = ${=p}^\circ$.
The exterior angle at $D$ of triangle $MDA$ equals the sum of the two opposite angles, so angle $MDE$ = ${=p}$ + ${=p}$ = ${=2*p}^\circ$.
$ME = MD$ (radii), so triangle $MED$ is isosceles and angle $MED$ = angle $MDE$ = ${=2*p}^\circ$.
Since $D$ lies between $E$ and $A$, angle $AME$ = angle $AMD$ + angle $DME$ = ${=p}$ + ${=180-4*p}$ = ${=180-3*p}^\circ$.
notes: Text-only version of book 5-c (figure not shown); asks for the whole angle AME. Check: angles of triangle MAE are p, 2p, 180-3p, sum 180. p in 12..40 keeps 4p<180.
